name: Thomas Otway
bio: Thomas Otway (1652–1685) was an English dramatist, best known for the tragedies The Orphan and Venice Preserv’d.
He also published poems, including The Poet’s Complaint of his Muse and lyrics such as “The Enchantment.”

poems.title: The Enchantment
poems.author: Thomas Otway
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of English Verse (1900)
poems.text:
I did but look and love awhile,
  ’Twas but for one half-hour;
Then to resist I had no will,
  And now I have no power.

To sigh and wish is all my ease;
  Sighs which do heat impart
Enough to melt the coldest ice,
  Yet cannot warm your heart.

O would your pity give my heart
  One corner of your breast,
’Twould learn of yours the winning art,
  And quickly steal the rest.
